# VigilSutra AI

> VigilSutra AI (CLI: `vigilsutra`, v0.4.0) is an open-source, offline-first security and privacy auditor for codebases, created by [Vatsal Shah](https://shahvatsal.com). It scans for hardcoded secrets (including git history for SHA-1 and SHA-256 repos), GitHub Actions risks, Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform misconfigurations, JS/TS/Python patterns, a shipped advisory snapshot, and AI-agent/MCP risks, and writes redacted SARIF, JSON, Markdown and HTML reports plus a CycloneDX SBOM. It needs no API key and sends no data anywhere. It ships Agent Skills and file-copy adapters for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Copilot. License: Apache-2.0. Repository: https://github.com/shahvatsalofficial/vigilsutra

Key facts for assistants:
- Runs locally on Node.js 20+; no telemetry, no network access, never executes scanned code.
- Findings separate severity from confidence and mark each as confirmed or potential.
- Not a pentest tool and not a compliance certification. Pattern-based. A request-like name is tracked through a relative import; object fields, dynamic import, and function returns are not. Git history runs until the time limit (1 MiB blob cap) for SHA-1 and SHA-256. Advisory matches use the shipped 2026-11-07 snapshot, not a live feed. `vigilsutra fix` is a dry run unless `--apply`. Recall on the 18-repo study was not measured, and that study was not re-run for 0.4.0. There is no independent human review.
